messages:
maria (oncall): :rotating_light: paging — several pods in gpu-pool-3 (us-west-2) are failing with CUDA OOM even though dashboard shows ~20% headroom across the node group. Customers reporting increased 5xx for generation endpoints.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1743126789 — autoscale/serving:cuda-oom (assigned to maria). PagerDuty notification sent.

samir (sre): saw the same, noticed repeated container crashes on node ip-10-2-8-19. Crash loop with OOM from CUDA allocator; container logs show allocation failures for ~50MB chunks.

ajay (infra): pushing up `nvidia-smi` and `dcgm` metrics now. Can anyone grab `kubectl logs` from one of the crashing pods?

maria (oncall): paste from logs:```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 52.00 MiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 29.10 GiB already allocated; 1024.00 MiB free; 512.00 MiB reserved in allocator)
```

nikki (ml): that message is interesting — shows 512MB reserved in allocator plus fragmentation leaving ~1GB free, but allocation of 52MB fails. Likely fragmentation + allocator reserved blocks not released. We recently deployed a model change that increases attention cache size on long contexts.

samir (sre): node-level `free`/`nvidia-smi` snapshot:```
GPU 0: 29.1 GiB used / 31.8 GiB total
Processes: 3 (our runtime + watchdog)
Cached memory reported by driver: 1.1 GiB
```Seems like the process has a large cache pinned.

ajay (infra): I'm seeing node flaps — kubelet restarted on ip-10-2-8-19 twice in last 10m. Suspect OOMs triggered container restarts causing fragmentation to blow up. I'll cordon and drain the node now to stop scheduling.

maria (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) cordon node, 2) restart affected pods sequentially to avoid simultaneous heavy allocations, 3) set env override on runtime to force smaller allocator split (`PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64`) for the canary pods, 4) if that holds, rollout env to pool.

ajay (infra): commands run:```bash
kubectl cordon ip-10-2-8-19
kubectl drain ip-10-2-8-19 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl rollout restart deploy/serving-runtime -l pool=gpu-pool-3 --field-selector metadata.name=serving-runtime-canary
```

nikki (ml): small note — `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64` reduces fragmentation risk by forcing fewer large free blocks. Also plan to add `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` calls post-request for long-live worker to reduce cached memory between requests as a short term.

samir (sre): applying env override to canary: `kubectl set env deployment/serving-runtime-canary PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64` — canary came back healthy for 15m with no OOMs. CPU/latency looks fine.

maria (oncall): customer impact: affected gen endpoints across 3 customers for ~12 minutes, degraded tail latency and ~8% 5xx. Post-mitigation error rate back to baseline for canary; rolling restart of pool in progress. Notifying SRE/CS.

ajay (infra): follow-up: kernel logs show repeated "device-side malloc failed" lines before driver reset. Also saw one case where reserved allocator blocks remained after process exit (we're on runtime v2.3.1). Opening infra ticket to bump runtime to v2.3.2 that includes allocator free-on-exit fix.

nikki (ml): action items for ML/runtime: - add guard to release large attention caches between requests for long-context models - add preflight allocation checks and fallbacks to smaller batch sizes when fragmentation detected - instrument allocator internal stats in metrics (reserved, active, free-fragments)

samir (sre): infra/temp mitigation: reduced default batch size for pool to 4 and enabled `max_split_size_mb:64` across the pool. Restart window complete. Monitoring for node flaps.

maria (oncall): handing off to ajay for next 2 hours for monitoring and customer comms. I'll update incident doc and attach timeline. @ajay please ack takeover.

ajay (infra): ack — taking over. Will keep node drained until runtime patch lands. Will coordinate with CS for targeted customer messages.

infra-bot: Incident update: INC-2026-1743126789 — mitigation applied (env override + batch limit). Status: monitoring.

maria (oncall): retrospective notes to add: fragmentation on allocator can manifest as OOM despite headroom due to reserved/fragmented blocks; container restarts exacerbate fragmentation; remediate by allocator config + code paths that free caches and avoid large contiguous allocations. Also consider kernel/driver upgrade if device-side failures persist.

samir (sre): will follow up with a small runbook snippet: quick mitigation sequence (cordon -> restart sequential -> set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` -> reduce batch size -> observe 30m) and postmortem if re-occurs.

nikki (ml): tagging infra ticket #INF-2746 and runtime issue #RT-918 for the free-on-exit fix and allocator metrics.

maria (oncall): closing initial page. If anything pops in next 30m, ping this thread and re-open. :white_check_mark:
